name: Core AI vocabulary, German
summary: German wordings of the English core glossary (core.json) and German-specific terms, in both tiers: `ai` (the term itself denotes AI) and `context` (wording around which AI is discussed or that stands in for AI, not proof by itself). It applies only to filings whose language is de, together with core.json, which matches the English terms these filings use as well (AI, machine learning, ChatGPT); English terms that German reports use unchanged are therefore not repeated here. Built by going through all 502 entries of core.json group by group and adding the German wording where one is in use, plus terms of German, Austrian and Swiss law and regulators. Every term is attested in a primary source (German text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, IATE, publications of BaFin, BSI, Datenschutzkonferenz, Bundesnetzagentur and FINMA, German statutes and EU legal acts in German, parliamentary and expert-body reports, German-language annual reports, industry-association and research papers, vendor pages for product names, and business press) or in the sample reports in gs://airo-eu-sample-reports; wordings whose hits in annual reports were mostly not about AI were demoted to `context` or removed. Inflected forms are listed as variants, because the plural suffix that glossary.py adds is the English one; abbreviations are case-sensitive. Swiss ss spellings of words with ß are listed as case-sensitive variants (lowercase-initial and capitalized), because glossary.py treats ß and ss as the same phrase and would otherwise drop the second spelling. A phrase with a suspended hyphen ("Text- und Data-Mining") cannot be matched by glossary.py and is not listed. Status: to be checked by a native speaker.
